nodes.title: Build a voiced, story-driven pinball game powered by a slot machine (chapters 1-2)
nodes.prompt:
Lets make a game.

I want to have something kind of interesting.

It should tell an epic, longform, final-fantasty style tale.

But it should have the game be "played" by a pinball machine that is powered by a slot machine giving credits to play the game.

Make it emotionally captivating, have complex adult concepts such as economics and balances of power and law, and tie that all into the story.

make this play out as the user plays pinball with voice and all

start by making the first two chapters.

For a story think a combination of FFVIII and FFX with a hint of metal gear solid political hijinks

[follow-up] make it with a functional core and an imperative shell. Use whatever tools allow you to work fastest on the best game
use a workflow to parallelize what you can

nodes.title: Zero-build vanilla ES modules + Canvas 2D + WebAudio, node --test for the core
nodes.description: No dependencies; core is plain pure functions testable headless in node; shell is the only code touching DOM/audio/time.

nodes.title: Game framework (Phaser/Matter.js) with bundler
nodes.description: Ready-made physics and rendering, but physics would live inside an imperative engine, defeating the functional core.

nodes.title: Voice via browser speechSynthesis only
nodes.description: No assets, but unreliable timing and no audio effects.

nodes.title: Voice pre-rendered with macOS say into audio files, speechSynthesis as fallback
nodes.description: Deterministic, distinct voices per character, can be routed through WebAudio for radio-filter codec calls.

nodes.title: Vanilla ES modules with a pure update(content, game, msg) core over a framework; pre-rendered say voices over live speechSynthesis
nodes.description: User asked for functional core / imperative shell. An Elm-style reducer returning effects-as-data keeps physics, slot, economy and story testable in node with no browser; a framework's physics engine would own mutable state. Pre-rendered voice files give reliable timing and allow a radio filter for codec-style calls.

nodes.title: Direction: full cinematic cutscenes; corporate and government espionage intertwined with community-trust missions
nodes.description: Folded into the design as: a full-screen cinema mode separate from the cabinet view; every scene tagged duty/covert/commons; a Trust stat earned by commons missions that funds mutual-aid balls (the Commons gives, the Mint lends at interest).
nodes.prompt: it should shift into showing full cutscenes and stuff too, get people emotionally invested, and have it be centered around espionage at a corporate and government level intertwining with missions to build community and trust

nodes.title: Write the shared contract (src/core/types.js), story bible and content index, then fan out the build to parallel agents
Story premise too close to FFX: replace pilgrimage-and-sacrifice with a treaty vote carried by a citizen drawn by lot
nodes.description: Dropped: shrine pilgrimage, chosen sacrifice, memory-eating tide, the cycle-is-a-lie reveal. New spine: islands linked by stillsalt-burning lights; the Mint decides who goes dark; a Tribune drawn by lot tours seven cities and casts the vote that renews or lapses the peace treaty; Halcyon rigged the draw and has bonded the outcome. Element ids, cast ids and backdrop keys unchanged so code built in parallel stays valid.
nodes.prompt: the story is too close to FFX

nodes.title: Direction: extend to chapters 3-5; ending turns on one powerful man's single delusion and can go either way
nodes.description: Corvane's delusion: people cannot be trusted with the truth. Two endings (The Lane Held / The Sum) decided by cumulative trust earned versus loans taken across all chapters. Chapters 3-5 outlined (Halcyon Reach, Little Brand, Tallis) and seeded toward it; 6-8 not yet written.
nodes.prompt:
keep it going from here then build more chapters

make there be an unwinding of the incentives and what matters at the end being due to someone with power having one cursed delusion that undoes them

but maybe make it so it can end either way

nodes.title: Replace chapters 1-2 with the treaty story, add chapters 3-5, and extend tables, backdrops, music and the ending ledger
Two-chapter build runs end to end in headless Chrome: 106/106 tests, 546 voice files, bot plays both chapters (median 23 min)
nodes.description: Verified by the integrator's browser run and screenshots, which I inspected. Not verified: real-time keyboard play beyond a brief check, audio by ear, HiDPI/resize, other browsers. Ramp/orbit scenes were too hard for the bot at 3 shots and were cut to 2.

nodes.title: Fold the slot machine into the pinball table and make iPhone portrait the primary layout
nodes.prompt:
okay so the slot machine should actually be part of the pinball game itself and give buffs/new balls/etc and credits to keep playing and have like elements you hit that fill it in and also elements that make it full spin
and also make the game most playable on portrait orientation on an iphone

nodes.title: Reels live on the playfield: top lanes fill one reel each, saucer and ramp shots spin all three, plunger is the lever when no ball is loaded
nodes.description: No separate slot screen. Paytable and economy (marks, loans, garnish) are kept; lever pulls cost marks, in-play spins are earned by shots.

nodes.title: Keep the separate slot screen and add an in-play mini slot
nodes.description: Less rework but two slot machines, and the user asked for it to be part of the pinball game itself.

nodes.title: Reels on the playfield with lane-fill and shot-spin over a separate slot screen
nodes.description: Matches the request directly (elements that fill it in, elements that full-spin), removes a mode switch that is awkward on a phone, and keeps the debt/commons economy intact by making the plunger the paid lever.

nodes.title: Rebuild core, cabinet, cinema and shell: reels on the playfield (lane-fill, armed spin shots, plunger as lever) and a portrait-first touch layout
nodes.description: Preceded by outcome: five-chapter build live on GitHub Pages at 140/140 tests, 1435 voice lines, old slot-screen landscape shape.
